blocks.text: Easter Island is one of the most mysterious places on the planet. The Polynesian settlers who reached it more than a thousand years ago created the Rapa Nui culture, leaving behind countless traces of their genius, above all the giant Moai statues. In three days of private excursions, discover the crater of Rano Kau and the Birdman village of Orongo, the quarry of Rano Raraku, Ahu Tongariki, the beach of Anakena and the sunset platforms of Tahai.

Day 1 · Meeting at the airport and transfer to your hotel. Then depart for the ceremonial centre of Orongo. Climb the slopes of the Rano Kau volcano to a viewpoint on the edge of the crater, which holds a beautiful lake with its characteristic vegetation.

Visit the ceremonial village of Orongo, where the island’s chief was chosen for a whole year through a perilous competition: every spring, the clans gathered in its stone houses, awaiting the arrival of the sacred Manutara bird to choose the Tangata Manu, the Birdman. Duration: 4 hours.
Vegetation-covered crater lake of Rano Kau by the ocean, Easter Island, Chile
Rano Kau on Easter Island: crater lake with the ocean beyond its slope

Day 2 · Breakfast, then a full-day tour of the island. Along the south coast, see unrestored platforms: Ahu Vaihu in Hanga Te’e Bay and Akahanga, said to be the burial place of the legendary king Hotu Matua. Continue to Rano Raraku, the quarry where most of the Moai were carved: of the nearly 900 statues on the island, some 397 still lie or stand on the slopes of this extinct volcano. Box lunch in nature.

Visit Ahu Tongariki, the largest platform on the island, with 15 restored Moai, then drive east to Ahu Te Pito Kura and the “Navel of the World”. End at Anakena Beach, with its warm turquoise water, white sand, palm trees and the Ahu Nau Nau platform, one of the most beautiful landscapes on the island: time for a walk and a swim. Return to Hanga Roa through the centre of the island.
Palm trees above the pale sand and turquoise water of Anakena Beach, Easter Island, Chile
Anakena: a palm-fringed ocean beach backed by green hills

Day 3 · Breakfast, then drive to the restored Ahu Akivi platform in the centre of the island, whose seven Moai are said to represent the seven explorers sent to Rapa Nui by King Hotu Matua. See the unrestored Ahu Hanga Puku Riki, then visit Puna Pau, a green and picturesque site whose red tuff, quarried from the slope of the extinct volcano, was used to carve the topknots of the stone giants.

End at the Tahai ceremonial complex, with its three platforms from north to south: Ko Te Riku, with restored eyes, Tahai and Vai Uri, part of Rapa Nui National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Duration: 4 hours. Transfer to the airport.
